note: The English teen edition quotes the KJV in each chapter's epigraph; every French epigraph is Louis Segond (1910) verbatim (only French spacing before : ; ! added, a final « ; » or « : » closed with a full stop), and the “(KJV)” label was dropped as in a-retrospect-teens.fr. Where the KJV quotes only part of a verse, the French quotes the matching Segond span (Jeremiah 6:16 without its last clause, Genesis 2:17 up to « du mal », Romans 12:2 first half, Nehemiah 8:10 last clause opened with « … »); Matthew 18:3 keeps Segond's « Je vous le dis en vérité » because the clause cannot start mid-sentence.

Psalm 19:1 (English numbering) is Psaume 19:2 in Segond, so the ch. 5 epigraph cites « Psaume 19:2 » and the reading suggestion « Psalm 19:1–6 » becomes « Psaume 19:2–7 »; the reference row keeps the English number.

All Chesterton quotations are rendered fresh in French (none is taken from a published French translation of Orthodoxy); puns were re-made rather than translated: « tout perdu, excepté sa raison » (lost everything except his reason), « laisser son époque n’en faire qu’à sa tête ; le difficile, c’est de garder la sienne » (let the age have its head / keep one's own), « À cheval ailé donné, on ne regarde pas les dents » (winged horse in the mouth), lévitation/« légèreté » (levitation/levity), « se prennent à la légère », and « la petite vitrine du païen » for “the small publicity of the pagan”. Reviewer: check these read as natural French wit.

Children's “Do it again!” is « Encore ! Recommence ! » and God's word to the sun is « Recommence ! » (also the ch. 5 title); the reader is addressed with « tu » as in the other teen editions, while Chesterton's generic “you” inside his quotations is « on » or « vous ». Title « Orthodoxie (Pour ados) » is 22 characters.
